xmldoc.short_description: Read an EDF, EDF+, BDF or BDF+ file into the neutral struct.

param_input_item.param_description: the path to the EDF, EDF+, BDF or BDF+ file.
the ordinary signals to keep, by label (a char or a cellstr) or by index; by default every ordinary signal.
a logical: 'Annotations' whether to parse the annotation channel (true by default), 'Data' whether to read the samples (true by default).

param_output_item.param_description: the neutral struct: the header, one entry per ordinary signal at its own rate in physical units, and the annotations.

description.p: The one reader of the EDF, EDF+, BDF and BDF+ binary format. It returns a domain-free struct: nothing in it assumes leads, sleep events or any other interpretation.

A stored integer becomes a physical value by physical = (digital - dmin) * (pmax - pmin) / (dmax - dmin) + pmin. EDF stores each sample in two bytes (signed int16), BDF in three (signed int24); both are little-endian. The whole data block is read in one pass and reshaped, because a night at 250 Hz is over a hundred million values.

The returned struct has the fields file, type ('EDF', 'EDF+', 'BDF' or 'BDF+'), family, continuous, version, patient, recording, startdate, starttime, startDateTime, reserved, records, duration, ns, signals (a struct array with label, transducer, unit, prefilter, physicalMin, physicalMax, digitalMin, digitalMax, samplesPerRecord, rate and data) and annotations (a struct array with onset, duration and text).

The annotation channel is never returned as a signal; it is a byte stream carrying time-stamped annotation lists (TALs). Each text becomes an annotation with its onset in seconds; the time-keeping stamp that opens each record has an empty text and carries none.

xmldoc.bibliography: Kemp and Olivan, European data format 'plus' (EDF+), Clinical Neurophysiology 114(9), 2003; Kemp et al., A simple format for exchange of digitized polygraphic recordings, Electroencephalography and Clinical Neurophysiology 82(5), 1992; BioSemi data format (BDF).
